ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::14: Imbalances in the gut microbial community (dysbiosis) of vertebrates have been associated with several gastrointestinal and autoimmune diseases. The specific bacterial taxa that drive gut dysbiosis remain poorly characterized across different host species. Different anatomical regions of the gastrointestinal tract may exhibit varying degrees of vulnerability to microbial disruption. Developmental stages during early life could present critical windows when dysbiosis is more likely to establish. Non-model organisms have received insufficient research attention despite growing evidence that gut microbiota profoundly influence overall health outcomes. We examined microbiome alterations during dysbiosis across multiple gastrointestinal compartments in ostriches (Struthio camelus), which are long-lived birds experiencing substantial juvenile mortality. The study analyzed 16S rRNA gene sequences from ileum, cecum, and colon tissues collected from 68 individuals that succumbed to suspected enterocolitis within their first three months. Age-matched controls consisted of 50 healthy individuals that underwent euthanasia for comparative analysis. Longitudinal sampling of environmental sources and fecal material enabled identification of where pathogenic bacteria originated. Developmental timing of when dysbiosis-associated microbes first appeared could be determined through this temporal sampling approach. Diseased individuals exhibited dramatically reduced microbial alpha diversity compared to controls across all three gastrointestinal regions examined. Beta diversity patterns also showed substantial divergence between diseased and healthy birds throughout the entire gut. The inverse correlation between diversity and disease remained strong across all age groups specifically in the ileum. Cecum and colon tissues showed weakening associations between low diversity and disease as birds matured. Enterobacteriaceae, Peptostreptococcaceae, Porphyromonadaceae, and Clostridium genera showed positive associations with mortality outcomes. Lachnospiraceae, Ruminococcaceae, Erysipelotrichaceae, Turicibacter, and Roseburia taxa correlated with healthy status. Food sources showed no contamination with dysbiosis-associated bacterial lineages. Water supplies similarly lacked pathogenic microbial signatures. Soil substrate contained no detectable dysbiosis-related bacteria. Fecal samples collected repeatedly revealed that pathobionts colonized ostrich guts immediately following hatching. These opportunistic microbes underwent population expansion specifically in hosts harboring low overall microbial diversity. Mortality events occurred multiple weeks after initial pathobiont colonization. Understanding how pathobionts first enter neonatal hosts represents a crucial research priority. Determining which factors promote diverse microbiota establishment could illuminate dysbiosis prevention strategies and healthy development pathways.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::17: The diffuse very high-energy (VHE, > 100 GeV) gamma-ray emission observed in the central 200 pc of the Milky Way by H.E.S.S. was found to follow the dense matter distribution in the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) up to a longitudinal distance of about 130 pc to the Galactic Centre (GC), where the flux rapidly decreases. Recent sensitive H.E.S.S. analysis revealed that the cosmic-ray (CR) density profile drops with the distance to the centre, making data compatible with a steady cosmic PeVatron at the GC. In this paper, we extend this analysis to obtain for the first time a detailed characterisation of the correlation with matter and to search for additional features and individual gamma-ray sources in the inner 200 pc. Our study utilizes 250 hours of H.E.S.S. observational data combined with improved analysis techniques. We perform a detailed morphology study of the diffuse VHE emission observed from the GC ridge and reconstruct its total spectrum. The emission correlated with dense matter covers the full CMZ. The flux from matter-correlated emission represents approximately half the total diffuse emission flux measured. Some emission at higher latitude likely originates from hadronic collisions of CRs in less dense regions of the GC interstellar medium. An additional emission component centred on the GC extends over about 15 pc. This component is consistent with the existence of a strong CR density gradient. The presence of a CR accelerator at the very centre of our Galaxy is confirmed by these observations. The spectrum of the full ridge diffuse emission is compatible with the one previously derived from the central regions. A single population of particles fills the entire CMZ, as suggested by spectral consistency. We report the discovery of a VHE gamma-ray source near the GC radio arc. The newly discovered source is produced by the pulsar wind nebula candidate G0.13-0.11. This identification adds to the inventory of point sources in the Galactic Centre region and demonstrates the capability of current instruments to resolve discrete objects within complex diffuse backgrounds.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::16: Cardiac disease and clinical intervention may both lead to an increased risk for thrombosis events due to modified blood flow in the heart, and thereby a change in the mechanical stimuli of blood cells passing through the chambers of the heart. Platelet activation levels depend on the magnitude and characteristics of mechanical stresses present in circulating blood. Our study focuses on computational analysis of left ventricular hemodynamics using patient-specific anatomical data. The Navier-Stokes equations govern the fluid dynamics within the ventricular chamber. Mitral valve flow is represented through a parameterized mathematical framework that captures the valve's opening geometry. Finite element discretization provides the numerical solution from which velocity and pressure fields are obtained. The velocity gradient tensor undergoes triple decomposition to isolate three distinct kinematic components. Rigid body rotation represents one mode of fluid motion in this decomposition scheme. Irrotational straining constitutes the second fundamental flow pattern. Shear deformation forms the third independent component of the velocity gradient. These three flow structures impose mechanically distinct stimuli on suspended blood cells. Simulations incorporating mitral valve clip intervention demonstrate substantial alterations in ventricular flow patterns. Quantitative comparison reveals differential responses among the three kinematic components following clip placement. Shear components exhibited disproportionately larger increases relative to rotational and strain components in clipped cases. One particular case showed a 64 percent reduction in effective valve opening area. This geometric change produced a 90 percent elevation in both rotation and strain magnitudes. The same intervention resulted in a 150 percent increase in shear magnitude, demonstrating non-proportional scaling. The disproportionate shear increase suggests specific mechanical activation pathways for platelets. Patient-specific computational workflows can simulate proposed interventions before clinical implementation. Detailed flow analysis provides quantitative metrics for comparing treatment options. Such computational frameworks could enhance risk stratification protocols for thrombotic complications. The methodology supports evidence-based clinical decision-making regarding cardiac interventions. Future applications may include optimization of device placement and sizing for individual patients.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::19: Hypertension can lead to mood disorders that may worsen or ameliorate depending on the type of antihypertensive prescribed. Depression is associated with modifications in basal brain asymmetry particularly that of the frontal cortex, which is involved in blood pressure control. Different vasoactive drugs may change the brain's asymmetry in a manner that contributes to cognition status. We studied the bilateral activity of several neuropeptidases in frontal cortex as a reflect of the functional status of certain neuropeptides involved in mood. Using arylamide derivatives as substrates, we fluorometrically analysed the activity of these enzymes in the left and right frontal cortex of control untreated Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) and spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs). We compared their activities with WKY or SHR treated with the antihypertensive drugs captopril (CAP) and propranolol (PRO). Additional comparisons included animals treated with the hypertensive agent N (G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester. Systolic blood pressure (SBP) measurements were obtained from all experimental groups to confirm their cardiovascular status. Untreated WKY exhibited normotensive values of SBP as expected for this strain. WKY treated with CAP or PRO maintained normal blood pressure levels. SHR treated with CAP also exhibited normotensive values of SBP. WKY treated with N (G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester demonstrated hypertensive values of SBP. Untreated SHR showed elevated blood pressure consistent with their genetic background. SHR treated with PRO and N(G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester also demonstrated hypertensive values of SBP. Changes in the bilateral distribution of neuropeptidases depended on the strain, the enzyme analysed and the drug used. Normotensive WKY groups revealed intrahemispheric correlations mainly in the left hemisphere. WKY treated with N(G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester demonstrated intrahemispheric correlations mainly in the right hemisphere. SHR groups also showed correlations predominantly in the right hemisphere. Interhemispheric correlations were mostly observed in WKY groups. SHR groups with antihypertensive treatments (CAP, PRO) also exhibited interhemispheric correlations. Our results suggest specific brain bilateral patterns of neuropeptidase activities in WKY that change in SHR. This observation may be related to the cognitive disorders that have been described in these animals under antihypertensive or hypertensive drug treatments.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::18: These international clinical practice recommendations (CPR) for developmental coordination disorder (DCD), initiated by the European Academy of Childhood Disability (EACD), aim to address key questions on the definition, diagnosis, assessment, intervention, and psychosocial aspects of DCD relevant for clinical practice. The development process involved systematic literature reviews combined with formal expert consensus methods to answer key questions across five distinct areas. Literature searches on mechanisms, assessment, and intervention were updated to include all relevant studies published since the previous 2012 recommendations. Completely new literature searches were conducted specifically for psychosocial issues and for adolescents and adults with DCD, areas not comprehensively covered previously. The Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine framework was used to rate all evidence according to levels 1 through 4. Two face-to-face meetings brought together an international, multidisciplinary expert panel to discuss areas where research evidence was insufficient. Five additional Delphi rounds were completed to achieve consensus on good clinical practice recommendations where empirical data was lacking. The final document contains thirty-five recommendations in total. Eight recommendations derive directly from empirical evidence identified in the literature reviews, with three addressing assessment and five addressing intervention. Twenty-two recommendations represent updates or modifications of recommendations that appeared in the 2012 version. Two new good clinical practice recommendations address diagnosis and assessment procedures. Three new good clinical practice recommendations focus specifically on psychosocial issues affecting individuals with DCD. Active video games are now recommended as useful adjuncts to traditional activity-oriented and participation-oriented interventions, based on emerging evidence. Two recommendations specifically target adolescents and adults with DCD, a population previously underserved in clinical guidelines. The CPR-DCD provides clinicians and scientists from varied disciplines with comprehensive, current understanding of DCD. National healthcare systems can adapt these international recommendations to create country-specific guidelines. The guidelines represent the first international effort to provide evidence-based recommendations for adolescents and adults with this condition.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::20: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the value and efficacy of rapid response teams (RRTs) for different triggering events in total hip arthroplasty (THA) patients. A retrospective review of all RRT events at a single, tertiary referral center from 2014 to 2016 was performed. Inclusion criteria were defined as patients >18 years old that underwent primary or revision THA. Information queried included demographics, primary reason for RRT, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), underlying etiology, whether any changes in management occurred, and whether the patient was uptriaged. In total, 168 RRTs were called on 153 hip arthroplasty patients (mean age 65.2 ± 14.1 years; mean body mass index 32.3 ± 4.8, 66% female). Length of stay in RRT for primary THA was 3.4 days. Revision THA patients requiring RRT stayed 6.2 days. Primary THA patients without RRT had a 2.4-day length of stay (P < .001). Revision THA patients not requiring RRT stayed 4.6 days (P = .005). There were no mortalities among any patients in the study cohort. RRTs for hypotension/presyncope (11%) resulted in significantly fewer changes in management (P < .01) than tachycardia (77%). Syncope (11%) also led to fewer management changes compared to hypoxia (57%). AMS triggered management changes in 79% of cases. Other triggers resulted in management changes 47% of the time. Hypotension/presyncope led to uptriaging in only 28% of patients. Syncope resulted in uptriaging 15% of the time. Hypoxia caused uptriaging in 30% of cases. Tachycardia resulted in significantly more uptriaging at 81% (P < .001). Hypotension/presyncope was found to be significantly more commonly due to volume depletion at 67% (P < .001). Hypoxia was significantly more commonly due to atelectasis in 57% of cases (P = .037). Opioids/oversedation caused hypoxia in 30.4% of patients. AMS/delirium was significantly more commonly caused by opioids/over-sedation at 71% (P < .001). The most common etiologies were potentially preventable through improved perioperative protocols and patient monitoring strategies.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::22: We aim to determine the redshift of GDS-1408, the most solid z~7 galaxy candidate lying in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field. We have used all the VLT spectra of GDS-1408 collected by us and two other groups with FORS2 at VLT in the last five years, for a total integration time of 52hr. The combined spectrum is the deepest ever obtained of a galaxy in the Reionization epoch. We do not detect any emission line or continuum over the whole wavelength range, up to 10100A. Based on an accurate set of simulations, we are able to put a stringent upper limit of f(Lya)<3x10^(-18) erg/s/cm2 at 3-9 sigma in the explored wavelength range. This flux limit corresponds to a rest-frame equivalent width EW<9A. Combining this limit with the SED modelling we refine the redshift to be z=6.82+/- 0.1 (1-sigma). The same SED fitting indicates that GDS-1408 is relatively extinct with A1600~1. The dust corrected star formation rate is estimated at approximately 20 Msol/yr. The case-B recombination theory predicts an un-attenuated equivalent width for this galaxy. The comparison between this theoretical prediction and the observed upper limit provides a limit on the effective Lya escape fraction of f_(esc)^(eff)(Lya)<8%. We cannot rule out a major contribution of the inter/circum galactic medium in damping the line. A plausible interpretation is that GDS-1408 is moderately evolved and contains sufficient gas and dust to attenuate the Lya emission before it reaches the intergalactic medium. The redshift confirmation of even the best z~7 candidates is very hard to achieve with the current generation of 8-10m class telescopes unless the Lya or unusually strong rest-UV nebular emission lines are present. We show that both JWST and E-ELT will be necessary to make decisive progresses in this field. Currently, the increased redshift accuracy obtained with this kind of analysis makes ALMA an interesting option for the redshift confirmation of high-redshift galaxy candidates. Future multi-wavelength campaigns will benefit from these complementary approaches.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::23: The survival of Salmonella spp. as pathogen indicator in composting was studied. The inoculums technique was used to gives the known amounts of Salmonella spp. involved in composting. Two different inoculation methods were compared to evaluate their effectiveness in pathogen elimination. Sample A received the Salmonella spp. solution added directly into the compost material, allowing immediate contact with the composting substrate. Sample B used the vial technique, where Salmonella spp. solution was placed into a sealed container and inserted into the middle of compost material before starting the composting process. The conventional method for enumeration involves serial dilution followed by standard membrane filtration as recommended in PAS 100 and British Standard (BS EN ISO 6579:2002). This study was designed to investigate the relationship of temperature and contact material that may also involve in pathogen activation specifically to Salmonella spp. Previous research by Deportes et al. (1995) reported that exposure to an average temperature during composting of about 55-60°C for at least 3 days sufficiently kills the vast majority of enteric pathogens. The amount of Salmonella spp. and temperature for both samples was set as indicator to determine the survival of Salmonella spp. in direct and non-direct inoculums. Quantitative die-off rates for Salmonella spp. during composting were calculated from the experimental data. The results from laboratory scale composting study showed that after 8 days at temperatures reaching at least 66°C, Sample A achieved Salmonella spp. numbers below the limits required by UK compost standard PAS 100 (BSI, 2005). The standard mandates that finished compost must be completely free of Salmonella spp. for commercial use. Sample B still contained high amounts of Salmonella spp. even after composting for 20 days, demonstrating the protective effect of the vial barrier. Direct contact with compost material proved essential for effective thermal inactivation of the pathogen. The physical barrier created by the vial prevented adequate heat transfer and limited exposure to antimicrobial compounds produced during composting.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::21: Emergency medical services play a critical role in managing acute stroke cases. In December 2006, we created the TOYOTA prehospital stroke scale for tissue plasminogen activator intravenous therapy (TOPSPIN) to identify patients requiring t-PA treatment. The scale evaluates five clinical parameters: consciousness level, presence of atrial fibrillation, language function, upper limb motor function, and lower limb motor function. This investigation assessed a decade of TOPSPIN application in distinguishing ischemic from hemorrhagic stroke under real-world conditions. From December 2006 through January 2017, we prospectively collected data on consecutive patients transported by Toyota city ambulance services who underwent TOPSPIN evaluation. The study analyzed final diagnoses at hospital discharge, including ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, and stroke mimics. We calculated the positive-predictive value for actual stroke cases among those screened. The proportion of patients receiving recanalization therapies was documented. Clinical characteristics distinguishing hemorrhagic stroke, ischemic stroke, and non-stroke conditions were identified. The cohort included 1,482 consecutive patients evaluated during the study period. Stroke was confirmed in 1,134 patients, representing 76.5% of the total sample. Within the stroke group, 628 had ischemic events, 34 experienced transient ischemic attacks, and 472 suffered hemorrhagic strokes. Non-stroke conditions accounted for 348 cases (23.5%), including 80 seizure patients, 42 syncope cases, 27 hypoglycemia episodes, and 199 miscellaneous diagnoses. Among the 628 ischemic stroke patients, 130 individuals (20.7%) underwent intravenous recombinant t-PA administration, endovascular intervention, or combined treatment approaches. Ischemic stroke patients more frequently demonstrated atrial fibrillation, advanced age, reduced blood pressure readings, and lower overall TOPSPIN scores compared to hemorrhagic stroke patients. Multivariable logistic regression modeling revealed that atrial fibrillation presence independently predicted ischemic stroke with an odds ratio of 2.33 (95% confidence interval 1.61-3.40). The TOPSPIN represents a practical prehospital assessment tool incorporating cardiac rhythm evaluation. Identifying atrial fibrillation during emergency transport suggests increased likelihood of ischemic rather than hemorrhagic stroke etiology.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::24: BACKGROUND: Although race is associated with prostate cancer progression in early stage disease, once men have advanced disease, it is unclear whether race continues to predict a poor outcome. The authors hypothesized that, in an equal-access setting among patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) and no known metastases (M0/Mx), black men would receive imaging tests at similar rates as nonblack men (ie, there would be an equal opportunity to detect metastases) but would have a higher risk of metastatic disease. METHODS: In total, 837 men who were diagnosed with M0/Mx CRPC during 2000 through 2014 from 5 Veterans Affairs hospitals in the SEARCH (Shared Equal Access Regional Cancer Hospital) database were analyzed. Data on all imaging tests after CRPC diagnosis were collected, including date, type, and outcome. Multivariable Cox models were used to test associations between race and the time to first metastasis, first bone metastasis, first bone scan, second bone scan among men who had a negative first bone scan, and overall survival. RESULTS: Black men (n = 306) were equally as likely as nonblack men (n = 531) to receive a first and second bone scan after a diagnosis of CRPC. The risk of developing any metastases showed no statistically significant difference between the two racial groups. Bone metastases occurred at comparable rates regardless of race. Time intervals to receiving bone scans were similar across racial categories. Overall survival did not differ significantly by race in this cohort. All comparisons yielded P values exceeding .2, indicating no meaningful statistical differences. CONCLUSIONS: The lack of racial differences in the development of metastases and scanning practices observed in this study suggests that, once men have a diagnosis of M0/Mx CRPC, race may not be a prognostic factor. Efforts to understand prostate cancer racial disparities may derive greater benefit by focusing on the risk of developing prostate cancer and on the outcomes of men who have early stage disease. Cancer 2016;122:3848-3855. © 2016 American Cancer Society.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::25: We present deep Hubble Space Telescope single-star photometry of Leo A in B, V, and I filters. Our new field of view is offset from the centrally located field observed by Tolstoy et al. (1998) in order to expose the halo population of this galaxy. We report the detection of metal-poor red horizontal branch stars, which demonstrate that Leo A is not a young galaxy. Leo A is at least as old as metal-poor Galactic Globular Clusters which exhibit red horizontal branches. These particular clusters are considered to have a minimum age of about 9 Gyr. We discuss the distance to Leo A in our analysis. We perform an extensive comparison of the data with stellar isochrones to constrain stellar populations. For a distance modulus of 24.5, the data are better than 50% complete down to absolute magnitudes of 2 or more. We can easily identify stars with metallicities between 0.0001 and 0.0004 in the observations. Stars with ages between about 5 and 10 Gyr are detectable in their post-main-sequence phases. However, we lack the detection of main-sequence turnoffs which would provide unambiguous proof of ancient (>10 Gyr) stellar generations. Blue horizontal branch stars are above the detection limits of our observations. These blue stars are difficult to distinguish from young stars with similar colors and magnitudes. Synthetic color-magnitude diagrams show it is possible to populate the blue horizontal branch in the halo of Leo A. The models also suggest approximately 50% of the total astrated mass in our pointing should be attributed to an ancient (>10 Gyr) stellar population. We conclude that Leo A started to form stars at least about 9 Gyr ago based on multiple lines of evidence. Leo A exhibits an extremely low oxygen abundance, of only 3% of Solar, in its ionized interstellar medium. The existence of old stars in this very oxygen-deficient galaxy illustrates that a low oxygen abundance does not preclude a history of early star formation. This finding challenges assumptions about chemical enrichment requirements for primordial stellar populations.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::26: One goal of neuromorphic engineering is to create 'realistic' robotic systems that interact with the physical world by adopting neuromechanical principles from biology. Critical to this is the methodology to implement the spinal circuitry responsible for the behavior of afferented muscles. At its core, muscle afferentation is the closed-loop behavior arising from the interactions among populations of muscle spindle afferents, alpha and gamma motoneurons, and muscle fibers to enable useful behaviors. We used programmable very-large-scale-circuit (VLSI) hardware to implement simple models of spiking neurons, skeletal muscles, muscle spindle proprioceptors, alpha-motoneuron recruitment, gamma motoneuron control of spindle sensitivity, and the monosynaptic circuitry connecting them. The system emulated a pair of antagonistic afferented mammalian muscles acting on a joint via long tendons. Each muscle was simulated by 1024 alpha-motoneurones and 1024 gamma-motoneurones in the hardware implementation. The integrated system successfully maintained a joint angle during experimental trials. Stretch reflex responses were reproduced when the system drove the nonlinear biomechanics of an actual cadaveric finger. We explored numerous values and combinations of gamma-static and gamma-dynamic gains when driving a robotic finger. Some parameter combinations replicated specific human pathological conditions observed in clinical settings. We investigated the behavioral consequences of adopting three alternative models of isometric muscle force production. The dynamic responses to rate-coded spike trains produce force ramps that can be very sensitive to tendon elasticity. This sensitivity becomes especially pronounced at high force output levels. Our methodology produced the first example of an autonomous, multi-scale, neuromorphic, neuromechanical system capable of creating realistic reflex behavior in cadaveric fingers. This research platform allows exploration of mechanisms behind healthy sensorimotor function in the physical world by building them from first principles. The platform also enables investigation of pathological sensorimotor conditions through systematic manipulation of circuit parameters. The work serves as a precursor to fully autonomous neuromorphic robotic systems for real-world applications.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::28: Evidence details how cannabis can influence the use of other psychoactive substances, including prescription medications, alcohol, tobacco and illicit drugs, but very little research has examined the factors associated with these changes in substance use patterns. This paper explores the self-reported use of cannabis as a substitute for alcohol among a Canadian medical cannabis patient population. Data was derived from a survey of 2102 people enrolled in the Canadian medical cannabis program. The analysis focused on 973 respondents, representing 44% of the total sample, who reported using alcohol on at least 10 occasions over a 12 month period prior to initiating medical cannabis. Retrospective data on the frequency and amount of alcohol use before and after medical cannabis initiation allowed researchers to determine which participant characteristics and other variables were associated with reductions and cessation of alcohol use. The study revealed that 419 participants, comprising 44% of the subsample, reported decreases in alcohol usage frequency over 30 days. Additionally, 323 participants, representing 34% of respondents, decreased the number of standard drinks they consumed per week. A smaller group of 76 participants, accounting for 8% of the sample, reported complete abstinence from alcohol in the 30 days prior to the survey. Participants below 55 years of age showed greater odds of reducing alcohol use compared to older respondents. Higher rates of alcohol consumption in the pre-medical cannabis period were also associated with increased likelihood of reduction. An explicit intention to use medical cannabis specifically to reduce alcohol consumption was associated with significantly greater odds of both reducing and ceasing alcohol use altogether. Alcohol remains the most prevalent recreational substance in North America. The use of alcohol results in significant rates of criminality, morbidity and mortality across the continent. These findings may lead to improved health outcomes for medical cannabis patients specifically. The results also suggest potential overall improvements in public health and safety at the population level.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::27: Introduction and Objective: Patients presenting with a urinary tract infection combined with kidney or ureteral stones represent a urologic emergency requiring immediate intervention. These individuals typically stabilize quickly after initial treatment but must remain in the hospital pending urine antibiotic sensitivity test results. Our study sought to determine which clinical factors predict antibiotic resistance in patients requiring urgent urinary tract decompression for sepsis caused by obstructive urolithiasis. Such predictors could enable earlier hospital discharge with empiric oral antibiotic therapy. Methods: We retrospectively identified patients who received emergent urinary tract decompression for sepsis with an obstructing ureteral stone between 2014 and 2018. Two academic medical institutions provided the patient cohort for this investigation. All subjects underwent emergent ureteral stent placement as the decompression method. Broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics were administered to all enrolled patients following the procedure. We examined relationships between clinical parameters measured at initial presentation and the presence of resistance to at least one antibiotic detected in urine cultures. Statistical analysis employed the Wilcoxon test for continuous variables and Fisher exact test for categorical variables. Multivariate logistic regression incorporated all variables showing significance in the univariate analysis phase. Results: The final cohort comprised 134 patients meeting inclusion criteria. Urine cultures from 84 patients (62.7%) demonstrated resistance to at least one tested antibiotic agent. Univariate analysis revealed that patients harboring resistant organisms had significantly higher rates of previous ureteroscopy procedures. These same patients more frequently required postoperative intensive care unit-level monitoring. Bacteremia occurred more commonly in the resistant culture group. Hospital length of stay was significantly prolonged among patients with resistant infections. Multivariate analysis incorporating the significant univariate variables yielded only one independent predictor. Previous ureteroscopy remained the sole factor significantly associated with antibiotic resistance, conferring increased odds of 6.95 (p = 0.011). Conclusions: History of ureteroscopy represents a significant predictor of antibiotic resistance in this patient population across both analytical approaches. Clinical application suggests patients with prior ureteroscopy should await definitive culture results before discharge. Conversely, patients lacking ureteroscopy history may safely receive early discharge with empiric oral antibiotics. Prospective validation studies are needed to confirm this predictor's clinical utility.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::29: The delicate balance between spin-orbit coupling, Coulomb repulsion and crystalline electric field interactions observed in Ir-based oxides is usually manifested as exotic magnetic behavior. Here we investigate the evolution of the exchange coupling between Co and Ir for partial La substitution by Ca in La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$. A great advantage of the use of Ca$^{2+}$ as replacement for La$^{3+}$ is the similarity of its ionic radii. Thus, the observed magnetic changes can more easily be associated to electronic variations. A thorough investigation of the structural, electronic and magnetic properties of the La$_{2-x}$Ca$_{x}$CoIrO$_6$ system was carried out by means of synchrotron x-ray powder diffraction, muon spin rotation and relaxation ($\mu$SR), AC and DC magnetization, XAS, XMCD, Raman spectroscopy, electrical resistivity and dielectric permittivity. Our XAS results show that up to 25% of Ca substitution at the La site results in the emergence of Co$^{3+}$, possibly in high spin state. The introduction of larger amounts of Ca beyond this threshold leads to the increase of Ir valence instead. The competing magnetic interactions resulting from the mixed valences lead to a coexistence of a magnetically ordered and an emerging spin glass (SG) state for the doped samples. Our $\mu$SR results indicate that for La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$ a nearly constant fraction of a paramagnetic (PM) phase persists down to low temperature. This persistent PM behavior is possibly related to the presence of a small amount of Ir$^{3+}$ in the undoped parent compound. Anti-site disorder at Co/Ir sites may also contribute to the paramagnetic fraction observed. For the doped compounds the PM phase freezes below 30 K. Despite this freezing transition, there is still some dynamics associated with the SG phase at lower temperatures. The dielectric data obtained for the parent compound and the one with 25% of Ca-doping indicate a possible magnetodielectric effect. This coupling phenomenon is discussed in terms of the electron hopping between the TM ions. The anti-site disorder influences the magnetodielectric properties significantly. The distorted crystalline structure also plays a role in the observed magnetodielectric behavior.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::30: With the stringent requirements introduced by the new sixth-generation (6G) internet-of-things (IoT) use cases, traditional approaches to multiple access control have started to show their limitations. A new wave of grant-free (GF) approaches have been therefore proposed as a viable alternative. However, a definitive solution is still to be accomplished. In our work, we propose a new semi-GF coordinated random access (RA) protocol, denoted as partial-information multiple access (PIMA), to reduce packet loss and latency, particularly in the presence of sporadic activations. We consider a machine-type communications (MTC) scenario, wherein devices need to transmit data packets in the uplink to a base station (BS). When using PIMA, the BS can acquire partial information on the instantaneous traffic conditions. The base station employs compute-over-the-air techniques to estimate the number of devices with packets waiting for transmission in their queue. Based on this knowledge, the BS assigns to each device a single slot for transmission. Since each slot may still be assigned to multiple users, collisions may occur. Both the total number of allocated slots and the user assignments are optimized, based on the estimated number of active users, to reduce collisions. This optimization improves the efficiency of the multiple access scheme. To prove the validity of our solution, we compare PIMA to time-division multiple-access (TDMA) and slotted ALOHA (SALOHA) schemes. TDMA represents the ideal solution for orthogonal multiple access (OMA) in the time domain under low traffic conditions. SALOHA serves as the optimal approach when high traffic conditions prevail. We show that PIMA is able to adapt to different traffic conditions. The protocol provides fewer packet drops regardless of the intensity of packet generations. PIMA merges the advantages of both TDMA and SALOHA schemes. This combination delivers performance improvements in terms of packet loss probability. The system also achieves reduced latency compared to conventional methods.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::31: Background and purpose — Bone remodeling as a response to bone trauma, postoperative immobilization, and device-related bone reactions can lead to loss of bone stock and increase the risk of periprosthetic fracture and aseptic loosening. This study investigates the adaptive bone remodeling of the proximal tibia after uncemented total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Patients and methods — We performed a 2-year follow up of 53 patients with mean age 62 years, ranging from 38 to 70 years. The cohort included 27 male participants. All patients received an uncemented TKA in a randomized controlled trial with bone mineral density (BMD) as secondary endpoint. Randomization allocated patients to 2 groups of either monoblock (A) or modular (B) polyethylene design. The TKAs were performed using the uncemented Zimmer Nexgen trabecular metal. Measurements of BMD were done postoperatively and after 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. Three regions of interest (ROI) were defined for BMD measurement. Results and interpretation — In group A statistically significant changes in BMD were seen after 24 months in both the medial and lateral ROI. BMD decreased medially by 15% (p = 0.004). Lateral BMD decreased by 13% (p = 0.01). In group B the BMD changes were limited throughout the observation period. After 24 months group B returned to the preoperative values. The differences in BMD change between groups were statistically significant in both the medial (p = 0.03) and lateral (p = 0.02) ROI. In the distal ROI we found no significant change in BMD in either group. A significantly different bone remodeling pattern of the proximal tibia was seen in the 2 groups. A higher degree of bone loss occurred in the knees that received the monoblock polyethylene design. The flexible monoblock implant design had previously been shown to improve fixation. However, this design does not decrease the bone loss of the proximal tibia.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::32: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are bio-inspired models of neural computation that have proven highly effective. ANNs lack a natural notion of time, which limits their biological plausibility. Neural units in ANNs exchange analog values in a frame-based manner, creating computational and energetic inefficiency. Biological neurons communicate sparingly using binary spikes, contrasting with the continuous-valued activations of artificial networks. Artificial Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) can be constructed by replacing ANN units with spiking neurons. Current SNNs perform far below deep ANNs on challenging benchmarks. These SNNs use much higher firing rates compared to biological counterparts, which limits their efficiency gains. We demonstrate how spiking neurons employing efficient neural coding can construct SNNs matching high-performance ANNs. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art SNN results on important benchmarks while requiring lower average firing rates. Spike-time coding based on firing rate limiting adaptation phenomenon provides the foundation for our method. This adaptation phenomenon occurs naturally in biological spiking neurons. Adapting spiking neuron models can capture this phenomenon mathematically. We derive the effective transfer function for these adaptive neuron models. ANNs trained with this transfer function allow direct substitution with adaptive spiking neurons. The resulting Adaptive SNNs (AdSNNs) perform inference in deep neural networks using up to an order of magnitude fewer spikes than previous SNNs. Adaptive spike-time coding enables dynamic control of neural coding precision during operation. A simple arousal model in AdSNNs further halves the average required firing rate beyond baseline improvements. This arousal concept naturally extends to other forms of attention mechanisms in neural networks. AdSNNs represent a novel and efficient model for neural computation with strong theoretical foundations. The architecture naturally fits temporally continuous applications where timing matters. Asynchronous processing becomes feasible with this event-driven computational framework. The energy efficiency gains make AdSNNs promising for neuromorphic hardware implementations.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::33: Context. LQ Hya is one of the most frequently studied young solar analogue stars. Between 2003 and 2009, observations revealed a coherent spot structure migrating in the rotational frame, as documented by various authors. Since that time, the star has entered a chaotic state where coherent structures seem to have disappeared. Rapid phase jumps of the photometric minima now occur irregularly over time. Aims. The SOFIN/FIES long-term monitoring campaign has tracked LQ Hya for 25 years. We present new temperature maps for the star covering the period 2006--2017. These maps document the chaotic state of the star. Methods. We employ a Doppler imaging technique to derive surface temperature maps from high-resolution spectra. Results. The mean temperatures extracted from the Doppler maps reveal a weak but systematic increase in the surface temperature of the star. This temperature rise is consistent with the simultaneously increasing photometric magnitude. During nearly all observing seasons we detect a high-latitude spot structure which is clearly nonaxisymmetric. The phase behaviour of this structure is very chaotic but agrees reasonably well with the photometry. Equatorial spots are also frequently seen in our observations. Many of these equatorial spots we interpret to be artefacts due to the poor to moderate phase coverage. Conclusions. The spot topology has remained very similar to the higher activity epochs even during the chaotic phase. Higher activity epochs featured more coherent and long-lived spot structures than currently observed. High-latitude and equatorial spot activity continue to characterize the star. The mid latitude range still being most often void of spots, as in previous epochs. We attribute the erratic jumps and drifts in phase of the photometric minima to changes in the high-latitude spot structure. The equatorial spots do not appear responsible for these phase variations. Our findings suggest that high-latitude features dominate the photometric variability during chaotic phases.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::34: Hydrogenation reactions are expected to be among the most important surface reactions on interstellar ices. However, solid state astrochemical laboratory data on reactions of H-atoms with common interstellar ice constituents are largely lacking. The goal of our laboratory work is to determine whether and how carbon dioxide (CO2), formic acid (HCOOH) and acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) react with H-atoms in the solid state at low temperatures. We also aim to derive reaction rates and production yields for these processes. Pure CO2, HCOOH and CH3CHO interstellar ice analogues are bombarded by H-atoms in an ultra-high vacuum experiment. The ices are monitored by reflection absorption infrared spectroscopy during the experiments. Reaction products are detected in the gas phase through temperature programmed desorption. This technique allows us to determine the destruction and formation yields. The corresponding reaction rates can also be calculated from these measurements. Within the sensitivity of our set-up we conclude that H-atom bombardment of pure CO2 ice does not result in detectable reaction products. Similarly, HCOOH ice shows no detectable products when exposed to H-atoms. The upper limits on the reaction rates are less or equal to 7e(-17) cm^2/s for both species. These low rates make it unlikely that CO2 and HCOOH play a major role in the formation of more complex organics in interstellar ices through H-atom reactions. In contrast, CH3CHO does react with H-atoms under the same experimental conditions. At most 20% of acetaldehyde is hydrogenated to ethanol (C2H5OH). A second reaction route leads to the break-up of the C-C bond. This fragmentation forms solid state CH4 with approximately 20% yield. The same pathway produces H2CO and CH3OH with combined yields of 15-50%. Methane most likely evaporates partly after formation due to the high exothermicity of the reaction. The reaction rates for CH3CHO destruction depend on ice temperature. Ice thickness does not influence these destruction rates.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::35: The methodology of funnel control was introduced in the early 2000s, and it has developed since then in many respects achieving a level of mathematical maturity balanced by practical applications. Its fundamental tenet is the attainment of prescribed transient and asymptotic behaviour for continuous-time controlled dynamical processes encompassing linear and nonlinear systems described by functional differential equations, differential-algebraic systems, and partial differential equations. Considered are classes of systems specified by structural properties - such as relative degree and stable internal dynamics - of the systems only, the precise systems' data are in general unknown. The absence of precise data reflects real-world conditions where complete mathematical models remain unattainable. Prespecified are: a funnel shaped through the choice of a smooth function and freely chosen by the designer, a fairly large class of smooth reference signals, and a system class satisfying certain structural properties. The designer selects these elements before implementation begins. The aim is to design, based on the structural assumptions and the input and output information only, a single `simple' control strategy -- called the funnel controller. This controller applies uniformly to any system of the given class and to any reference signal. Application results in feasibility of the funnel control objective: that is solutions of the closed-loop system do not exhibit blow-up in finite time. All variables are bounded throughout operation. Most importantly, the evolution of the error between the system's output and the reference signal remains within the prespecified funnel boundaries at all times. The Introduction describes the genesis of funnel control, tracing its historical development. Subsequently, we investigate diverse system classes amenable to funnel control through detailed analysis. Funnel control is shown for systems with arbitrary relative degree, extending beyond traditional limitations. Systems described by partial differential equations also fall within the framework. Input constraints impose practical limitations that must be addressed. Applications demonstrate the methodology's effectiveness across industrial domains.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::36: With the increasing diversity of Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks, it is becoming extremely challenging to design a fully protected network. Stealthy Link Flooding Attack (SLFA) is a variant of DDoS attacks that strives to block access to a target area by flooding a small set of links. Traditional DDoS defense mechanisms are unable to detect or prevent SLFA attacks effectively. Moving Target Defense (MTD) techniques dynamically change network settings to confuse and deceive attackers. This dynamic reconfiguration makes it highly expensive for adversaries to launch a successful attack. MTD implementation introduces operational overhead to the network infrastructure. Determining the optimal timing and extent of MTD application represents a major challenge for network administrators. The attacker's behavior patterns significantly influence defensive strategies but remain difficult to predict accurately. This research addresses the challenge of obtaining the optimal MTD strategy that effectively mitigates SLFAs while minimizing operational costs. The problem is formulated as a signaling game with the network defender and the attacker as competing players. Signaling games are mathematical models where players have incomplete information about each other's types or intentions. A belief function is established and updated throughout the engagement between the attacker and defender during the SLFA campaign. This belief system enables each player to select the best response or action based on observed behaviors. Game-theoretic analysis yields equilibria that represent stable strategic configurations. A defense mechanism is derived directly from these equilibrium solutions. The evaluation uses a Mininet-based network environment for realistic testing conditions. An attacker performs SLFAs while a defender applies MTD based on the calculated game equilibria. Experimental results demonstrate that the signaling game-based dynamic defense mechanism provides protection levels comparable to extensive MTD solutions. The proposed approach achieves significantly reduced overhead compared to continuous or aggressive MTD deployment. This efficiency gain makes the defense strategy practical for real-world network environments with resource constraints.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::37: Multi-fidelity (MF) methods are gaining popularity for enhancing surrogate modeling and design optimization by incorporating data from various low-fidelity (LF) models. Adaptive sampling methods that dynamically allocate resources among fidelity models can achieve higher efficiency in exploring and exploiting the design space. Most existing MF methods rely on the hierarchical assumption of fidelity levels. Many approaches fail to capture the intercorrelation between multiple fidelity levels for quantifying the value of future samples. We propose a framework hinged on a latent embedding for different fidelity models and the associated pre-posterior analysis to explicitly utilize their correlation for adaptive sampling. Each infill sampling iteration includes two steps in this framework. The first step identifies the location of interest with the greatest potential improvement using the high-fidelity (HF) model. The second step searches for the next sample across all fidelity levels that maximize the improvement per unit cost at the previously identified location. A single Latent Variable Gaussian Process (LVGP) model makes this approach possible. The LVGP maps different fidelity models into an interpretable latent space to capture their correlations without assuming hierarchical fidelity levels. This model enables us to assess how LF sampling candidates will affect HF response with pre-posterior analysis. The framework determines the next sample with the best benefit-to-cost ratio through this analysis. Test cases demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms benchmark methods in both MF global fitting (GF) and Bayesian Optimization (BO) problems. The method achieves superior convergence rate compared to existing approaches. Robustness is another key advantage of the proposed framework over traditional methods. The framework offers flexibility to switch between GF and BO by simply changing the acquisition function. This adaptability allows practitioners to address different optimization objectives without restructuring the underlying model architecture.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::38: Cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum are secondary lesions induced by significant increases in cytokine levels in the brain. The comparison focused on SAH patients who developed cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum versus those who did not. We further compared patients who achieved good outcomes with those who had poor outcomes. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to identify risk factors for poor clinical outcomes. We analyzed 159 SAH patients in total. Among these patients, 17 individuals (10.7%) had cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum. Patients with these lesions were more likely to be in a severe condition according to World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies grading IV-V (odds ratio [OR], 4.53; 95% confidence interval [95% CI]: 1.60-12.84; p = 0.0042). Multivariate analysis confirmed that cytotoxic lesions increased the risk of poor outcome (OR, 4.39; 95% CI: 1.06-18.1; p = 0.037). The development of these lesions may be related to the extent of hematomas in SAH patients. Although cytotoxic lesions are usually reversible, they may serve as predictors of poor outcomes in SAH patients.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::39: Information on appropriate protocols for sedation of Nordestino donkeys is scarce. This study aimed to evaluate the sedative and cardiorespiratory effects of low doses of intravenous (i.v.) xylazine with and without acepromazine in 'Nordestino' donkeys. HHAG remained below baseline for 30 min in SX0.5 and AX0.5 groups. All treatments with xylazine increased VAS scores in situ for 15 min after xylazine administration. ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::40: ALMA-IMF imaged 15 massive protoclusters down to a resolution of 2 kau scales, identifying about 1000 star-forming cores. The mass and luminosity of these cores, which are fundamental physical characteristics, are difficult to determine, a problem greatly exacerbated at the distances >2 kpc of ALMA-IMF protoclusters. We combined new datasets and radiative transfer modeling to characterize these cores. Mass-averaged temperature estimates were calculated for the entire population. The derived temperatures enabled us to infer core masses using standard dust opacity assumptions. Bolometric luminosities were measured for approximately 1/6 of the sample. Deblending corrections were implemented when multiple sources overlapped in the observational data. Our methodology employed spectral energy distribution (SED) analysis through the PPMAP Bayesian procedure. PPMAP preserves the finest angular resolution available in the input observations. The algorithm generated luminosity and dust temperature images at 2.5" resolution across the survey fields. A second relationship connected external heating rates to the temperatures of prestellar cores. Our analysis yielded dust temperature estimates for 883 cores throughout the ALMA-IMF survey. Hot cores displayed systematically lower temperatures than previous studies using complex organic molecules as thermometers. We constructed a mass-luminosity evolutionary diagram at core spatial scales for high-mass protostars. This diagram represents the first such analysis combining fine spatial resolution with a statistically large sample. The observational results suggest protostars accrete from mass reservoirs exceeding their immediate core environments.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::41: The aim of the present study was to investigate the role of microRNA (miR)-27a-3p in osteoarthritis (OA). Interleukin (IL)-1beta-treated primary human chondrocytes were also analyzed for these molecular markers. ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::42: Space weathering is a process that changes the surface of airless planetary bodies. Prime space weathering agents are solar wind irradiation and micrometeoroid bombardment. These processes alter planetary reflectance spectra and often modify their compositional diagnostic features. In this work we focused on simulating and comparing the spectral changes caused by solar wind irradiation and by micrometeoroid bombardment to gain a better understanding of these individual space weathering processes. We used olivine and pyroxene pellets as proxies for planetary materials. To simulate solar wind irradiation we used hydrogen, helium, and argon ions with energies from 5 to 40 keV and fluences of up to $10^{18}$ particles/cm$^2$. To simulate micrometeoroid bombardment we used individual femtosecond laser pulses. We analysed the corresponding evolution of different spectral parameters, which we determined by applying the Modified Gaussian Model. Principal component analysis was conducted as an additional analytical method. The original mineralogy of the surface influences the spectral evolution more than the weathering agent. Olivine showed diverse spectral slope evolution upon irradiation. Pyroxene exhibited a different pattern of spectral slope changes compared to olivine. The spectral slope changes seen in olivine are consistent with observations of A-type asteroids. The moderate to no slope changes observed in pyroxene are consistent with asteroid (4) Vesta. Ions simulating solar wind have a smaller influence on longer wavelengths of the spectra than laser irradiation simulating micrometeoroid impacts. The different penetration depths of ions and laser pulses most likely explain this wavelength-dependent effect. Ions penetrate only the uppermost surface layers of mineral samples. Laser pulses can affect deeper material through shock wave propagation and thermal effects. Our results suggest that in some instances it might be possible to distinguish between the contributions of the two agents on a weathered surface.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::43: HEALPix by Górski et al. (2005) is the de-facto standard for Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data storage and analysis. Current and upcoming CMB experiments rely heavily on this framework for their observational data processing. The Legacy Archive for Microwave Background Data Analysis (LAMBDA) predominantly stores its datasets in HEALPix format. Visual representation of astronomical data serves as a critical component in modern astrophysical research workflows. The original Fortran facilities provided the first tools for rendering HEALPix maps. Python integration through the healpy package expanded accessibility to a broader scientific community. Modern GPU architectures now possess sufficient computational power to render extremely large astronomical maps without perceptible latency. Consumer devices such as laptops and tablets can now perform real-time visualization tasks previously requiring workstation hardware. The HEALPix Viewer application targets the macOS operating system exclusively. Metal framework integration enables direct access to GPU computational resources for maximum performance. The software compiles natively on both Intel x86_64 and Apple Silicon Arm64 processor architectures. Interactive data exploration workflows benefit from reduced latency and improved responsiveness. Publication-quality cartographic output can be generated with minimal time investment. Direct drag-and-drop functionality integrates seamlessly with Keynote presentation software. Microsoft PowerPoint also supports the same drag-and-drop workflow for cross-platform compatibility. Standard spherical projections including Mollweide, orthographic, and equirectangular are available by default. Multiple scientific colormaps ship with the application for different visualization requirements. Open-source availability allows researchers to extend functionality according to specific project needs. Benchmark comparisons against Python-based tools show performance improvements ranging from 3x to 180x across different computational tasks.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::44: To compare the cervical shear wave elastography (SWE) by using transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) between twin and singleton pregnant women. Baseline characteristics were similar between groups except for maternal age, with twin pregnancies averaging 33.1±4.6 years compared to 29.9±5.4 years in singleton pregnancies (p-value = 0.006). The upper cervical point measurements showed no significant differences at mid-trimester. Early trimester measurements at both upper and lower cervical points were comparable between groups. Twin pregnancies delivered at 35.9±2.8 weeks compared to 37.6±2.9 weeks for singleton pregnancies (p-value = 0.008). Spontaneous preterm delivery occurred in 22.2% of twin pregnancies and 15.8% of singleton pregnancies (p-value = 0.483). The cervical SWS might be an additional option for monitoring the change in cervical softness in twin pregnancies.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::45: Chromosome number is a key feature of the higher-order organization of the genome, and changes in chromosome number play a fundamental role in evolution. Dysploid gains and losses, along with polyploidization events, may drive reproductive isolation and lineage diversification. Mayrose et al. (2010) developed ChromEvol, which introduced probabilistic models for studying chromosome number evolution. Their groundbreaking work enabled inference of ancestral chromosome numbers over molecular phylogenies. This methodology generated new interest in studying the role of chromosome changes in evolutionary processes. The ChromEvol approach assumes all changes occur anagenetically, meaning they happen along branches of the phylogenetic tree. ChromEvol does not model events that are specifically cladogenetic, occurring at the splitting of lineages. Cladogenetic changes may be expected if chromosome alterations result in reproductive isolation between nascent species. We present ChromoSSE, a new class of models that incorporate both anagenetic and cladogenetic change in chromosome number evolution. The ChromoSSE models allow determination of the mode of chromosome number evolution across different scenarios. We can assess whether chromosome evolution occurs primarily within lineages or primarily at lineage splitting events. Clade-specific combinations of both modes can also be detected and characterized. The models enable estimation of the location and timing of possible chromosome speciation events over the phylogeny. We implemented ChromoSSE in RevBayes, a Bayesian statistical framework for phylogenetic inference. This implementation accommodates uncertainty in parameter estimates while leveraging likelihood-based methods. We tested ChromoSSE's accuracy through simulation studies before applying it to empirical datasets. We re-examined chromosomal evolution in five plant groups: Aristolochia, Carex section Spirostachyae, Helianthus, Mimulus sensu lato, and Primula section Aleuritia. Our analyses found evidence for clade-specific combinations of anagenetic and cladogenetic dysploid modes. Polyploid modes of chromosome evolution also showed clade-specific patterns in these taxonomic groups.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::46: We present results of our time variability studies of Mg II and Al III absorption lines in a sample of 22 Low Ionization Broad Absorption Line QSOs (LoBAL QSOs) at 0.2 <= zem <= 2.1 using the 2m telescope at IUCAA Girawali Observatory over a time-scale of 10 days to 7.69 years in the QSO's rest frame. ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::47: The H{\alpha} nebular emission line is an optimal tracer for recent star formation in galaxies. JWST has enabled observations of this line at z>3 for the first time. We present a catalog of 1013 H{\alpha} emitters at 3.7<z<6.7 in the GOODS fields obtained from a blind search in JWST NIRCam/grism data. The FRESCO survey provides 124 arcmin^2 of observations in GOODS-North and GOODS-South with the F444W filter, probing H{\alpha} at 4.9<z<6.7. ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::48: Numerous studies have revealed that oxidative stress is closely associated with the occurrence and development of depression. *This is the end, isn't it?*

The thought struck Josh suddenly, almost by accident. His frustration with the broken-down car evaporated in an instant. The phone company's failure to build towers along this remote stretch had left him completely isolated. The merciless sun had beaten him into exhaustion hours ago. None of these grievances seemed to matter anymore.

*This is the end.*

He realized he had already seen Heather for the last time without knowing it. Joey had recently aced his geometry test and wouldn't stop bragging about it. Dale was set to inherit the family business next year. That business would become an unexpected legacy for their entire community.

*This is it.*

Dale had warned him this trip was a fool's errand before he left. His friend had even joked about delivering a eulogy at Josh's funeral. The irony of that conversation now felt crushing. Yet even this dark memory couldn't dislodge the central thought taking root in his consciousness.

*The end of...*

Time became impossible to measure as Josh sat there motionless. His mind's contents began draining away like water through a sieve. Memories, worries, and plans all receded toward some distant horizon. Only one idea remained fixed at the center of his awareness.

*This is the end of me.*

Josh found a strange appropriateness in this thought being his final one. It seemed almost poetic that finality itself would be the last thing he contemplated.

But it wasn't.

The thought vanished as abruptly as it had arrived.

Josh would have wept if his body still responded to his will.

His regrets returned in a devastating flood. Anger surged through him with renewed intensity. Sorrow pressed down on his chest like a physical weight. His powerlessness in the face of death felt unbearable. The brief tranquil peace had been shattered completely. He confronted the reality of a life left incomplete. Nothing had been properly resolved or reconciled. His existence had failed to achieve any meaningful closure.

Then Josh felt **fear**. This terror exceeded anything he had previously experienced. Fate itself seemed to loom before him as a tangible presence. The great unknown yawned open, revealing his complete lack of preparation. This overwhelming horror consumed every other sensation and thought simultaneously.

That fear was the last thing Josh experienced.

"Why not?" She asked quietly.

In an age of wireless devices and ubiquitous information, we lifted our gaze from our screens only to see the sky ignite, consumed by a cold, variegated blaze. The phenomenon lasted only a few hours. The entire world witnessed it within minutes of its appearance. People immediately desired closer contact with the gentle flame. They wanted to touch it, to experience its caress directly.

Then they flew. Their flight carried them far and fast through the air. Others swiftly joined the first fliers in the sky. They began to fall, very slowly at first. Like boats taking on water, they sank further as more people joined them. The correlation between flying population and descent rate became obvious quickly. Flying was not the only supernatural ability available to us. Before the Shine faded, many such abilities manifested themselves. Flight, strength, healing, invisibility, immortality, teleportation, and speed appeared among the population. These common abilities disappeared very quickly. Some initially believed the powers were temporary, linked to the Shine's duration. The truth was that power potency was inversely proportional to the number who selected each ability.

More obscure powers started cropping up after this realization. Salarymen decided they wanted to excrete gold. Children chose to control animals. Before six hours had passed, truly bizarre phenomena began. Temperature plummeted rapidly in certain areas. The ground shook with increasing frequency. Clocks stuttered and stopped unpredictably. Mass death followed these events. Four billion people perished in twelve hours. An eight-billion-strong global society of Earth's most intelligent species collapsed completely. We dissolved into groups and factions focused solely on survival. Those without powers became kings in this new order. People with obscure, uncopyable powers became gods in flesh. Desperate populations worshipped these powerful individuals.

Several days passed before conditions stabilized somewhat. During this period, the sun crossed the sky only once. Weather patterns became completely erratic and unpredictable. Cities were nearly deserted, abandoned by most inhabitants. Only larger and more powerful factions could maintain urban habitation. Humanity went from pursuing prosperity to living rough within twenty-four hours. We reverted to bestial behavior, though retaining slightly more intelligence. Many possessed supernatural abilities on top of this regression.

Considerable time has elapsed since the Shine touched our sky. Humanity has established many new settlements across the landscape. The most popular power options remain weak due to overselection. Death grants power in this new world order. Raids occur frequently and without mercy. The largest settlements possess the greatest collective strength. These major population centers serve as primary targets for smaller cliques. Cohabitation with others means perpetual warfare. The more peaceful among us chose to travel instead of settling. Nomadic life offered escape from constant violence.

I have done exactly that. My travels have taken me across vast distances. I have searched relentlessly for a solution to this madness. My goal has been restoring the world to its former sanity. The relative stability of the old world seems like paradise now. I may have finally discovered what I sought. The answer lies in an ancient structure I found yesterday. "And all of a sudden, a rock flew out of nowhere and hit my poor husband in the head," she continued.

He keeled over into the water immediately.

She had screamed for help, but he drowned before anyone could reach them.

Now of course I had already known it must have been something like this from the moment she walked in the door. I have an uncanny sense for things like that, a detective's intuition if you will.

I looked as grave as I could manage, given the circumstances. "I see," I said, blowing another perfect smoke ring up towards the ceiling. "And you would like me to find and prosecute the perpetrator of this event."

"Yes," said the dame simply.

"I will do my best, I can promise you that," I assured her.

I saw her visibly sigh with relief at my words.

"May I offer you a cup of tea? Something stronger, perhaps?" I offered hospitably.

"No thank you," she declined, and without another word she showed herself out.

I promptly made my way to the Brandywine River dock to begin my investigation. My first line of inquiry would be to interrogate the man who rented out boats there. An odd fellow, and an odd profession—not many sane hobbits choose to be out in the middle of the water by their own free will.

And indeed, this hobbit's boat-renting business was not doing well financially.

After a long consultation of his records he told me that he had rented out two boats on the evening in question. Only one of those rentals was by a couple, he specified.

The couple had been a one Drogo Baggins and a one Primula Brandybuck, according to his ledger.

Primula, that was the dame's name, I realized. But why had she not wanted to tell it to me initially?

Had this boat fellow heard any commotion on the water, any cries for help? No he had not, which struck me as peculiar.

Did he remember who returned the boat to him after the rental period? It hadn't been returned at all, he said. In fact, that particular boat had been left floating in the middle of the river, abandoned.

Strange indeed, I thought to myself.

Next I walked up and down both banks of the river, searching for clues. Not much to garner here, except that whoever had thrown the rock must have been quite a shot, given the distance involved.

Having thoroughly investigated the river scene, my next step was to find out about Primula and Drogo's personal lives. After visiting several pubs in the areas of Buckland and Hobbiton, I had gathered this information: Primula and Drogo were long married, though perhaps not happily from what the gossips said.

They had one son, now 12 years of age, named Frodo Baggins.

Strangely, it seemed that Primula had not been seen by anyone except me since Drogo's death three nights prior.

In fact, most of the gentlehobbits that I spoke with seemed to be of the belief that both Drogo *and* Primula had died three nights ago in the boating accident.

Facts were not adding up in my mind. Before I could do anything else, I had to speak with my mysterious client again so as to straighten things out. Though I had no way of contacting her directly, I knew she would return to my offices in short order.

The day following, she did just that, appearing at my door.

"Good day, Primula," I said upon her entrance, using her real name deliberately.

Her face betrayed surprise at my knowledge, but she did not deny the name or attempt to correct me.

"I have a few things I need to get straight with you about the case," I said, and proceeded to outline what I had discovered during my investigation. "So I'm afraid I must ask again," I finished firmly. "What happened that night?"

And without a word, the dame got up and left my office. Just like that, with no explanation whatsoever.

I did not hear from her again after that abrupt departure, and two days later, her body was found floating down the Brandywine River. I was saddened but not surprised by this tragic turn of events.

My suspicion had been this: having been unhappily married for some time, Primula had pushed her husband into the water herself. She had then boated back to the shore with the intent of disappearing forever from Hobbiton society.

Everyone would think that they both were dead in a tragic accident, and so would not suspect any foul play on her part.

However, upon eavesdropping on the lawyer's meetings that quickly followed Drogo's death, she realized that custody of her son would go to an extended cousin. That cousin was none other than the famous crackpot Bilbo Baggins, a most unsuitable guardian.

Understandably, Primula did not want her offspring to fall under the influence of said crackpot and his wild ways.

And so she came to me in the hopes that I would believe her fabricated story. She wanted me to deflect suspicion away from herself, all in a desperate attempt to maintain custody of her son through legal means.

But I, having seen through her ruse with my detective's eye, prevented this fact from remaining hidden. Seeing no alternative she then drowned herself in grief and despair.

Shame—I had just begun to think there may have been a very beneficial alternative arrangement for the both of us, if you catch my meaning.

I sat back and began polishing my pipe thoughtfully with a soft cloth. It was another case solved by the estimable Bertram Proudfoot, detective extraordinaire, but perhaps another opportunity lost in matters of the heart.

I had solved countless cases throughout my career, but opportunities of the romantic sort came only but now and again in a detective's lonely life.

Like I said, it was a shame and a waste.

I blew another smoke ring to the ceiling as my thoughts turned to crazed old Mr. Baggins and his eccentricities. I felt genuine sympathy for the young Mr. Frodo, who was now cursed enough to fall into the old hobbit's custody and care.

Who knows what peculiar ideas old Baggins would pass on to the impressionable young fellow during his upbringing.

As I'm sure you're all aware, Mr. Bilbo Baggins suddenly disappeared many years ago without explanation. He then returned just as suddenly a year later with hoards of gold and many tall tales of adventure.

Having been a very respectable hobbit before he left on his mysterious journey, whatever he experienced seemed to have addled his mind permanently.

He came back a changed hobbit, and not for the better in most respectable hobbits' opinions.

He was so changed, in fact, that it is my personal suspicion that the hobbit currently inhabiting Bag End is not the real Bilbo Baggins at all. Rather, I believe he is an impersonator who has assumed Bilbo's identity for unknown purposes.

There is plenty of evidence to suggest this theory if one examines the facts carefully. Particularly striking is the fact that "Mr. Baggins" appears much younger than a hobbit of his years has any right to look, defying natural aging.

His mannerisms have also changed dramatically from the old Bilbo that neighbors remember fondly.

I shall have to explore that line of inquiry further some day when time permits and another case presents itself.
