Bystanders gathered in a circle, watching without intervening. Dark scorch marks from previous immolations stained the stairs beneath her.

"Mommy, why is she on fire?"

"Oh, that's normal," my mother replied.

"So it is totally normal for people to burst into flames?" My six year old brain struggled to process this horror.

"The normalcy refers to the political climate, not spontaneous combustion," she explained. "Our nation is engaged in civil conflict right now." Citizens opposed to authoritarian rule choose self-immolation as their form of demonstration. The government has maintained iron control over every aspect of daily life for decades.

"Will she be okay?" I genuinely believed someone might save her from the flames.

"I don't know," came the haunting response.

Years later, after the civil war ended in defeat for the rebels, I discovered records of every person who had sacrificed themselves this way. Historical archives documented their names, ages, and final statements. My homeland's struggle for freedom had cost hundreds of lives through this particular method of protest.

During my university years, I researched the psychology behind such extreme acts of resistance. These individuals possessed convictions powerful enough to override the human survival instinct. Death by fire represented their final rejection of tyranny. They chose agency in their deaths over submission in their lives.

Revolutionary movements emerge cyclically throughout human history, appearing roughly once per generation. The downtrodden eventually recognize their subjugation and discover new technologies for coordination. Social networks, encrypted messaging, and digital organizing platforms shift the balance of power. Change typically requires decades of sustained effort and sacrifice.

Yet here I stood at twenty-seven, facing a future of guaranteed poverty and surveillance. The ruling party had perfected methods of population control that previous dictatorships could only dream of. Facial recognition cameras monitored every street corner now.

I returned to that same intersection where I had witnessed the burning girl twenty-one years earlier. Workers had scrubbed away all evidence of past protests from the marble steps. My childhood innocence had died along with thousands of freedom fighters. Three generations had suffered under this regime's boot, including my grandmother's cohort. Violence was their only language, so violence would be my reply.

I climbed the stairs and doused myself in accelerant. The match felt heavy in my trembling fingers.

Fire consumed my flesh within seconds, bringing agony beyond imagination. Through the orange haze and searing pain, I forced my eyes to remain open. A young girl stood exactly where I had stood two decades ago, her small finger pointing directly at my burning form.

I walked downstairs and opened up the digital screen. A banker popped up on the screen.

"Hello Mrs. Roer. How may I help you?"

"I'd like to check my bank statement. I got a letter in the mail that I only have five credits?"

"Okay, one moment." The banker disappeared for a second and then came back up.

"Mrs. Roer. You currently have 10 credits."

"What? That's not even enough to buy groceries with this month?"

I looked outside and then sighed.

"Okay. Well thanks." I said.

The screen closed after the banker wished me a good day. A gallon of milk costs 1.21 credits in our society's happiness-based economy. I couldn't afford even basic dairy products anymore.

I walked outside this time. The weather was sunny and bright that morning. Birds chirped cheerfully in the trees surrounding my property. I suspected those birds had more purchasing power than I did at this moment.

My in-ground pool sparkled in the sunlight. The hot-tub sat adjacent to it, unused for months. An outdoor deck extended from the back of the house. A decorative pond lay further from the main structure.

My husband and I had been married for ten years now. Our wedding had been featured in national magazines. The press had called us the happiest couple in the country back then.

I went to look at my phone for distraction. A message from my husband appeared on the screen.

'Want to have coffee?'

I sent back,'Yes.'

I went upstairs and took a shower. My husband was at our other residence, as he usually was these days. Our marriage had deteriorated significantly over the past three years. We once held the world record for accumulated happiness credits as a couple. His multiple extramarital relationships were documented by gossip columnists. I had remained faithful physically but emotionally felt disconnected for years now.

I prepared myself for coffee. I chose an outfit that struck a balance between formal and relaxed. We were only meeting for a brief conversation, after all.

I walked outside and got in one of our cars. The vehicle drove itself to the private airport we used. Our jet was already fueled and ready on the tarmac.

"Just having coffee today Bill," I said to our pilot.

The flight took four hours to reach the coastal city where my husband was staying.

"Hello Mrs. Roer," He said, kissing my cheek in his customary greeting.

I walked with him toward our vacation property. A blonde woman with a tight blouse was exiting through the front entrance. I glared at her with obvious contempt. She rushed to her vehicle and drove away quickly.

"We need to talk," I said.

"Exactly," He replied, his tone suggesting satisfaction at my discomfort.

"Listen, Mr. Roer, I do love you, but there's so --."

"Elaine, I want a divorce."

"That was quick." I said.

He shrugged dismissively.

I left immediately after that exchange. The promised coffee never materialized.

The return flight seemed shorter than the journey there. A bank notification awaited me when I landed. My happiness credits had dropped to zero, the system informed me.

An unexpected message from Luke appeared on my phone.

"Coffee?" It read.

"Sure." I answered.

My doorbell rang at that exact moment. Luke stood on my doorstep when I opened the door.

He immediately kissed me passionately. The sensation reminded me of feelings I'd suppressed for years. My heart raced in my chest.

"Good to see you."

"Listen Luke, I just-"

He kissed me again, interrupting my sentence.

"I paid your husband to let me marry you Elaine. He wanted the divorce anyway, and you deserve better treatment. Financial arrangements have already been finalized between us."

The revelation stunned me completely. Luke had purchased my freedom like a business transaction.

"Elaine. Our son needs his mother back in his life."

Tears began streaming down my face. I had abandoned Luke and our child to satisfy my husband's demands. My former spouse had forbidden any stepchildren in our household.

"Elaine. Marry me. Please?" He walked further inside my house. "Our son is waiting in the car. Reig is twelve years old now."

I had maintained contact with Reig until his fourth birthday. My husband's political ambitions had forced me to sever all communication after that.

I walked outside and Reig jumped from the vehicle. He embraced me tightly with both arms. My phone buzzed with another alert, possibly my ex-husband justifying his mercenary behavior.

The bank had deposited 20,000 happiness credits into my account.

"Yes. I'll marry you."

Saying that I "saw" it is misleading, it was more of a feeling than anything. For the brief moment in time when I saw that blur cut through the night, I knew it was over.

That night, they came.

Men in adaptable camouflage, armed with pulse rifles and sabers. They didn't even think twice before cutting down the people in our village. I'm lucky to have escaped with my life. And I owe it all to one AI. He was a maintenance bot that we had stolen from the federation. He mostly helped us cart around materials, but that day, he was truly a hero. In the midst of all the gunfire and explosions, the mess hall had come crashing down. I was among the unfortunate souls who ended up inside. It all happened in an instant, and before I even had time to react, I was laying trapped under a pile of rubble. Through the smoke and flames I could see him. A grizzled maintenance bot with the serial number SR-71 on his arm. His metallic silver eyes caught my gaze, and he immediately ran over to help me.

As far as I know, we're the only ones who made it out alive. We ran until I couldn't run anymore, and eventually I collapsed. As I lay there, clinging to the final threads of life, I just kept stammering to myself "Blackbird....Blackbird....Black.."

SR-71 leaned in real close, and whispered in my ear.

"The SR-71 was developed during the Cold War as a strategic reconnaissance aircraft." His voice was steady despite the chaos we had just escaped. "Lockheed's Skunk Works division designed it under Clarence 'Kelly' Johnson's leadership." The bot's optical sensors dimmed as he accessed his historical databases. "It could fly at altitudes exceeding eighty-five thousand feet." His metallic hand gripped my shoulder with surprising gentleness. "The aircraft's titanium skin could withstand temperatures over six hundred degrees Fahrenheit." I struggled to understand why he was telling me this now. The vastness of the pit really can't be put into words but for the sake of this journal i'll try my best. The rim extends further than the human eye should be able to see according to normal physics and yet i can make out tiny details on the far cliff face with unnatural clarity. It looks big enough that you could fit the whole Earth in and knock it around like an ice cube in the bottom of a bourbon glass, maybe even several Earths. Even while sitting in the cab of the rumbler i get vertigo looking down onto the levels below, my stomach lurching. If it wasn't for the special anti-psychotics the docs give us i'm sure what i see on the lower levels might have some lasting horrific effect on me, permanent madness perhaps. The crew and i wash down todays dose with a bottle of sacramental wine, the ritual bringing us comfort. Why not celebrate, today was a good day after all given where we are. Today we reached the edge of Limbo, the first circle of our descent.

Entry:49

Not much to record today, some minor skirmishes on the perimeter, just some low level demons taking a swipe at us. Otherwise nothing going on but general camp stuff, maintenance and supply checks mostly. The engineers are working double time to ensure the security of Limbo Base, welding and hammering around the clock. They say it'll be fully up in 2 days, i have my doubts about their timeline. After their fiasco at the river they've got a lot of face to save with the entire division. 2 Rumblers, 4 squads of troops and a Screacher lost because of their damn barges that capsized in the Acheron. Bastards cost us good men through their incompetence.

I Hate just sitting around like this with nothing to distract me from the oppressive atmosphere. The smell of rot and sulphur somehow filters into the rumblers cab despite the tech geeks assurances that the cab is perfectly hermetically sealed with triple redundancy. It feels like the smell is inside my skull rotting tiny holes in my brain, burrowing deeper with each breath. My dreams have been getting worse, filled with images of writhing bodies and screaming faces. The chaplain says this is normal for extended operations in Hell's territory, that prayer will shield my mind. I've been reciting the Lord's Prayer before sleep but it doesn't seem to help much anymore.

Entry:51

HOOAH! CONTACT BABY! Praise God i've been waiting for this moment since the first days of the war for the surface when we were still fighting in the ruins of Jerusalem. Hell finally saw fit to send us some worthy opponents AND WE KICKED THEIR MUTHA FUCKING TEETH IN!! HAHAHAHAHAHA, the adrenaline is still coursing through my veins as I write this!

They came a few hours after my last entry like a great black tornado rising from the depths. A swirling column of harpies, skrieks and imps beyond counting rising up from the center of The Pit and came crashing down completely enveloping Limbo Base in darkness. The first few moments of engagement should've been chaos but by the grace of God we were ready for their assault. All the Screachers had been on high alert since we emerged from the maze of caves and onto the plains of Limbo proper 8 days ago. Today that diligence paid off in ways that exceeded our wildest expectations.

The blitz of the winged demon assault crumbled before the wall of sound our blessed Screachers blasted out at maximum amplitude. The word of God is anathema to the denizens of Hell, scripture being poison to their very essence. The word of God pumped out through a mobile rig of high powered speakers piloted by a devout member of the clergy is down right debilitating to demonic forces. The shocked and paralysed Demons that twitched and writhed on the ground were easy targets for our secondary weapons. The rumblers blessed water cannons burning away swaths of the foul creatures as if the misted holy water were strong acid melting flesh. Huge piles of the creatures were reduced to ash in seconds, leaving only sulfurous smoke behind.

The larger Demon haridens proved more resilient to our sonic attacks and i saw more than a few grunts die on their talons. Their sanctified body armor was little better than cardboard against those razor sharp claws. We repaid them in kind and i'm proud to say our rumblers javelin cannons sent a good lot of the giant buzzards screaming into oblivion impaled on our gleaming silver spears. I should record the grunts efforts so it doesn't seem like i'm diminishing their contribution to the victory. Their bravery and ferocity in battle is remarkable, they've got that in spades even facing certain death. Despite the mortal danger they collected their fair share of scalps, pinning the giant creatures with their silver pikes. They finished them off with their chain sickles in brutal close combat that would make any warrior proud. It was a glorious bloody sight, like something out of a nature documentary about apex predators.

The greatest trial of the battle was yet to come though, a challenge beyond anything we'd trained for. After a full day and a half of fighting the black swarm began to thin out and we thought we might've finally broken their assault through sheer attrition. But then they appeared from the deeper levels, ascending like nightmares made flesh. Three monstrous figures coming into focus through the haze of ash and exhaustion that clouded the battlefield. Hell Dragons emerged, nothing like what we'd seen in movies or our stories from childhood about noble beasts. These were great pestilent, foul things that towered over us like mobile fortresses of corruption. Snub nosed heads the size of a grand cathedral covered in spines sharp as swords. Long armored bodies like an insects, segmented and chitinous beyond reason. Their faces and joints slick with thick black tar that bubbled and hissed as it fell from them. The tar stained the plains of Limbo wherever it touched, corrupting the ground itself.

Screachers focused their assault on the dragons and prevented the titans from over running the base through coordinated fire. The rumblers water tanks and javelin cannons ran dry just trying to keep them at bay, every shot counting. Our brave grunts held back the black swarm, fighting tirelessly which allowed us time to retreat. We resupplied and reentered the fray multiple times in a desperate cycle. And so it went for hours on end and for all our efforts the Hell Dragons seemed to be none the worse for our attacks. Salvation finally came at the hands of the engineering corps who redeemed themselves. Of all people, those same bastards who lost us men at the river! Through our efforts we had given them enough time to secure and assemble Limbo Bases major defenses finally. Sanctified Artillery and the Holy Rail Gun were brought online at last. The Rail Gun punctured the Dragons thick armor spewing geysers of tar onto the battlefield in fountains. The artillery smashed into the beasts vulnerable exposed points lodging shells etched with scripture deep in their bodies. The holy words wracked them with pain from the inside out, making them thrash and scream. The attack still went on for hours and we lost a great deal of our force in the prolonged engagement. After nearly 2 months since we first descended into this place we finally have established a forward base to launch our attack on Hell proper. One Bolgia down eight to go before we reach the center. This is the first day here that the smell doesn't bother me, victory making everything sweeter.

He used to hit me so much.

I'd never even had a drink, and he beat cracked ribs, bruised kidneys and loose teeth into me. His stated purpose was to make sure I never became what he was.

Once when he was sober he told me he drank because of how he grew up. He said it like he wanted me to empathise with him, to forgive him. My arm was broken from him protecting me from drink the week before. He couldn't see himself standing over me crying blood and snot and tears, jeering. He needed alcohol to let him sleep at night. It stopped him from waking up screaming. It prevented him from pissing himself when he had a bad dream.

He made me sick, my dad. My breath catches sometimes now. One of my wrists never set right, leaving me half crippled in that hand. I have eleven false teeth. I'm only twenty three years old.

I didn't go to his funeral. I celebrated it though. I could never take a drink. I cry myself to sleep most nights. I can't help myself screaming if someone comes up to me suddenly. Lately I've noticed a lot of blood coming up when I cough. I won't let him beat me though. I won't give him this little victory.

When my son was born it was the happiest day of my life. For the first time in my life, someone wanted and needed me. His mother left soon after that, saying she didn't want to be trapped in a lifestyle she didn't choose. She carried the child for nine months. She abandoned him in three weeks. During those nine months she never objected to that lifestyle.

Honestly, after she left it all got too much for me. I left my son with my mother for the night. I went and had a drink. It was perfect. It was the best I've felt in my whole life. For a few hours, I wasn't scared. I felt no self-loathing during that time. I wasn't on edge anymore. I felt just calm and ok. I could deal with everything a little better. I think I'll probably have a few more now. I want to keep the buzz going. Sobriety now scares me even more. I know that there's such an easy alternative. That alternative is so much better than what I had before.

When I picked my son up in the morning mom looked at me funny. I blew her off. I was in a bit of a rush. I'd heard good things about whisky. I was eager to try it.

But don't worry. I won't let my son grow up like I did. I'll make sure he knows alcohol is evil. I won't expose him to that pain. I won't expose him to that fear. I'll make sure he hates me for as long as possible. I'll make sure he hates me as much as possible. He'll associate alcohol with me. I'm bad, so he'll break the cycle. I'm not strong enough. He will be strong enough though. I know he'll be strong enough. I'll make him calloused enough outside. I'll make him cold and hard enough inside. He'll be able to beat it. I can't beat it myself.

The planet Earth has changed dramatically over recent decades, with the most significant transformation occurring 23 years ago when the surface storms finally ceased. These atmospheric disturbances had persisted for approximately five thousand years according to our historical records. A few weeks elapsed while the dense cloud formations gradually broke apart and dispersed into nothing. Humanity received its first unobstructed view of the planetary surface in millennia.

I was five years old when this momentous event occurred, and my attention was captured primarily by the vivid colours visible below. The stunning blue of the oceans and vibrant green of vegetation were completely unlike anything available aboard the Ark. Our water supplies existed only in small tanks and reservoirs insufficient to produce that rich azure hue. The hydroponics bays grew plants under suboptimal conditions that yielded a muddy, pale green rather than the brilliant emerald visible on the surface. My desire was to experience these wonders directly through physical contact and proximity.

That childhood longing probably motivated my decision to volunteer for the first journey recruitment programme years later. This expedition would mark humanity's initial return to the planetary surface after generations in orbit. Many citizens demanded immediate descent once the storms dissipated, organizing public demonstrations that sometimes escalated into violent confrontations. These protesters foolishly advocated for the Ark to commence landing procedures without delay or preparation.

Waiting 23 years might seem excessive, but caution was absolutely essential given the circumstances. Humanity's entire surviving population resided aboard the Ark, making any catastrophic failure a potential extinction event. Our scientists conducted extensive geological surveys from orbit for two decades. Low-altitude reconnaissance missions gathered additional data using specialized drones and atmospheric probes. These investigations identified an ideal landing location that met all our critical requirements. The site would cause minimal ecological disruption to the surrounding wilderness. Sufficient space existed for establishing a sizeable settlement with room for expansion. Natural resources including freshwater sources and edible flora were abundant throughout the region. Most crucially, the geography provided exceptional defensive advantages through newly-formed mountain ranges created by the Cataclysm and profound oceanic trenches containing water of the deepest indigo shade.

The Ark's massive size prevented it from simply descending and touching down on the surface without extensive preparation. Our expedition team would establish permanent residence planetside, becoming the first humans to do so in over seven generations. The primary objective involved constructing a massive docking facility capable of receiving the Ark safely. This construction project would require approximately five or six years to complete even under optimal circumstances. Beyond building, we would conduct detailed cartographic surveys of the surrounding territory. Studying the local ecosystem's plants and animals was another crucial research goal. The uncomfortable truth was that our mission involved venturing into largely unknown territory despite all the orbital reconnaissance. The Corps had designated our destination the "safe-zone," though it could easily prove lethal. Our shuttle lacked sufficient power to escape once we descended into this protected valley.

The planet's atmospheric conditions remained treacherous even after the great storms ended, with smaller weather cells still rotating violently. The surrounding mountain peaks shielded our landing zone from these residual tempests that lacked the strength to cross such high elevations. A ferocious wind current circulated constantly in the upper atmosphere layers. This airflow would shred any departing vessel smaller than the Ark into fragments. Only the Ark possessed sufficient mass and structural integrity to withstand these forces during ascent. The Ark required a completed docking facility to achieve escape velocity safely.

Our assignment was clear: descend, survive whatever dangers awaited, construct a monumental structure, complete everything within six years—and I felt absolutely thrilled.

Deep green eyes studied the Knight Whyte with concern. This dying warrior had served him faithfully for years.

Craig was walking home from the shops when he met God. The encounter was completely unexpected, as sane people rarely anticipate meeting deities. Craig had never devoted much thought to theological matters. He occupied a space between belief and disbelief, never committing to either position. Questions of faith held no interest for him whatsoever.

Caramels, however, commanded his passionate attention. These confections consist of multiple wafer layers enveloped in chocolate coating. Their deliciousness had captivated Craig completely. His devotion to these biscuits rivaled religious fervor in intensity. The sole purpose of his shopping expedition had been acquiring more Caramels. Thoughts of eating them consumed his mind during the walk home.

Two minutes remained before he would reach his house and satisfy his craving. A voice suddenly called his name. The interruption broke his pleasant anticipation. Craig turned to identify the speaker behind him.

A tall figure in a loose suit stood there. Their gender was impossible to determine with certainty. They resembled David Bowie during his Diamond Dogs period. Craig felt he recognized them from somewhere. The memory remained frustratingly elusive. Awkward silence stretched as he stared. He needed to say something appropriate.

"Hi," Craig offered uncertainly. "Do I know you?"

"In a way," the stranger answered. "I'm God."

"Well good for you," Craig responded dismissively. "I've got to get going now. Bye."

He pivoted toward his house immediately. Caramels awaited in his shopping bag. Wasting time on mentally unstable strangers held no appeal.

"Wait, don't go yet. Please," the person pleaded. "What would it take for you to believe me?"

Craig exhaled in frustration. Indulging this individual might actually expedite his return home. Sometimes cooperation proves faster than avoidance.

"I don't know," Craig replied wearily. "A miracle or something. Some extraordinary thing which couldn't just be done by any old person. Something more than just saying that you're god."

"Hmm. How about this!" God gestured toward a nearby bush.

The shrub erupted in flames instantly. Fire coalesced into a dragon shape. The creature roared menacingly at both of them. God snapped their fingers decisively. The inferno vanished completely. The bush remained standing, scorched but surviving. God faced Craig with outstretched arms in a triumphant pose.

Craig appeared moderately impressed by the display. He studied God with renewed interest.

"Yeah, that was pretty good. Looked very impressive. I have to admit I have no idea how you did it. A hologram maybe? It worked for Tupac, so I can see it working for a dragon."

God maintained eye contact for several seconds. Their expression suggested disbelief at Craig's skepticism.

"I did it by being God. You asked for a miracle. I showed you one. What more do you want from me?"

*** 
The Author 
*** 

A persistent unease has lodged itself in my consciousness. The sensation resembles invisible fingers tracing the vertebrae of my spine with deliberate slowness. Something malevolent has taken residence at the base of my skull, feeding on my awareness like a lamprey. I am being observed by an unseen presence. The certainty of this surveillance grows stronger each passing moment. An entity I'll refer to as the *author* monitors my every thought and action. He sits hunched over his desk at this very instant, transcribing my existence. His writing instrument bears the marks of nervous chewing, a habit he indulges during creative pauses. The pen moves across paper in an illegible scrawl that only he can decipher. His current project involves devising the circumstances of my demise. The methodology occupies his complete attention as he weighs various scenarios.

My predicament stems from my own relentless curiosity. Questions about existence consumed my waking hours for months. The possibility of a guiding intelligence behind reality became an obsession. Humanity's collective purpose, if such a thing existed, demanded investigation. Philosophy and theology offered unsatisfying answers to my fundamental inquiries. Then a revelation struck me with the force of a physical blow. The insight arrived unbidden during an ordinary Tuesday afternoon. Reality itself operates according to narrative principles rather than random chaos. Every event connects to others through invisible threads of causation and meaning. Stories require someone to tell them, an architect of events. Therefore, an *author* must exist to shape the unfolding drama of existence.

A yellow taxi-cab nearly ended my life yesterday evening. Pressure built in my chest cavity as though invisible hands were squeezing my ribs. The pedestrian signal displayed its green walking figure, granting me permission to cross. Instead, instinct commanded me to retreat from the curb. My body obeyed this inexplicable warning without conscious deliberation. The intoxicated driver never registered my presence on the sidewalk. His vehicle careened through the intersection at twice the legal speed limit. Metal met metal as the taxi collided with the traffic signal post. That pole had been mere inches from my previous position seconds earlier. The temporal sequence of events defied coincidence: first the metaphysical revelation, then an immediate threat to my survival. My eyes turned skyward in accusation toward the unseen manipulator. Rage and terror competed for dominance in my emotional landscape.

"What the actual fuck was that?" The words escaped my lips before prudence could intervene.

Admittedly, profanity directed at a deity-level entity demonstrates poor judgment. Death itself hung in the balance, justifying my lack of diplomatic finesse.

*Are you sure?* My rational mind attempted to introduce skepticism.

I evaluated my circumstances from multiple philosophical angles. The physical coordinates of my position held less significance than the metaphysical implications.

*Yeah, I'm fucking sure,* came my internal response. *Sudden enlightenment followed immediately by a murder attempt exceeds statistical probability. An* author *exists and prefers to remain unacknowledged.*

The *author's* gender registered as male through some inexplicable intuition. His desire for anonymity felt equally certain, transmitted through channels I couldn't identify. My genetic or spiritual composition apparently included receptors for this information. Religious frameworks fail to capture what I'm describing here. Survival, not salvation, motivates my analysis of these phenomena. The sky received my continued glare as I transmitted wordless fury upward. An unnatural groaning sound emanated from the damaged signal pole. My attention shifted from celestial accusations to immediate surroundings.

The metal structure had twisted into impossible angles from the impact. Flames now engulfed the taxi-cab, though I hadn't witnessed the ignition.

*When had that happened?* The question formed automatically. *Nevermind, run stupid.* Self-preservation demanded immediate evacuation.

My interior monologue tends toward harsh self-assessment rather than gentle encouragement. Flight seemed the logical response, though its ultimate utility remained questionable. An omniscient *author* embedded in my consciousness could track me across continents. Flashbacks could immobilize me in traffic at his convenience. Mack trucks exist in abundance throughout urban environments. Yet he hadn't finished me already, which suggested parameters governed his actions.

*Fuck me,* the realization crystallized. *It's about the drama; the story.* Narrative requirements constrained even the architect of reality.

"Sick fuck," I announced to the empty street. He would transcribe that insult in his cramped handwriting, recognizing its intended recipient.

*What if I stop?* Rebellion offered a potential strategy.

My face turned upward again for direct address. "What are you going to do with a character who won't cooperate, huh?" The challenge hung in the air unanswered.

Divine responses failed to materialize from the clouds above. Lightning strikes remained theoretical possibilities within his presumed capabilities. My awareness of his existence might constitute sufficient reason for elimination. Knowledge of the pattern threatened the integrity of his design.

*What the hell is the plan anyway?* The question demanded consideration.

Presumably, the plan culminated in my death through non-mundane circumstances. Ordinary mortality held no appeal for an artist of his caliber. Spectacular demise would justify the narrative investment in my character arc. That theory aligned with the evidence accumulated thus far. The warning sensation returned with renewed intensity, cramping my abdominal muscles. My intestines seemed to be attempting escape through my skin. The churning demanded another backward step, which I executed immediately. Sharp penetration violated the skin of my back between shoulder blades. The blade's entry felt smooth, almost surgical in its precision. Warm blood began its journey downward, mixing with perspiration. My flannel shirt absorbed the spreading wetness rapidly.

A feminine voice spoke directly into my ear canal. "Hello protagonist," she said. "I'm your antagonist, the *author* says hello." Her introduction contained no wasted words.

She offered no further explanation or justification. No perfume or body odor accompanied her presence. She existed as pure function, a shadow given temporary form. Her identity and selection criteria remained mysteries. But her message confirmed my theoretical framework completely. Vindication arrived simultaneously with my probable death. Take that fucker. The words formed in my mind though my vocal cords lacked strength. He heard them anyway, I'm certain.

-
To whoever is investigating my disappearance... In case I don't return.

No one knows when their turn will come. We quickly developed methods to predict its movement patterns and avoid contact. The phenomenon cannot be stopped by any means we have discovered. Marshall Law brought the worst containment attempts in our history. The isolation periods inflicted psychological trauma on everyone involved. One iso-man asked me whether universal survival created a worse outcome than death would have. He wondered if interacting with people we had selfishly quarantined was morally unbearable. "Would it have been best if the moment caused death instead?" His eyes locked into mine with disturbing calmness. My face showed panic and guilt while his displayed complete serenity. The moment had already passed through him, leaving him safe. I remained vulnerable to its approach.

We have identified several rules governing the moment's behavior. The first rule states it only affects men exclusively. Every male human falls within its target range. Age provides no immunity whatsoever. The second rule indicates its intent is not lethal in nature. Deaths have occurred among the very young and elderly populations. Medical intervention can prevent fatalities in most cases. The third rule establishes it affects men on a singular basis only. One man experiences the moment at any given time. No simultaneous experiences have been documented in any region. The fourth rule shows its movement follows proximity patterns. Standing near someone experiencing it increases your probability of being next. The fifth rule proves no physical barrier can contain it. Isolation of infected areas ultimately failed in every attempt. Once the moment cycled through all males in the quarantine zone, it continued spreading outward. The sixth rule confirms it can be outrun through sustained movement. Its speed matches that of an average human walking pace. The seventh rule describes the experience as involving extreme physical pain.

As to where I went and why.

I was asked what I thought the moment could be when research began. I claimed something scientifically explainable must be causing it. Observations led to hypotheses, which led to experiments conducted month after month. We tested for viruses, bacteria, parasites, and mass hysteria without success. Nothing in our scientific framework could account for it. When people suggested aliens or divine punishment, I laughed dismissively. I proclaimed science would inevitably find the answer through rigorous methodology. Eventually no answer emerged from any research avenue. I experienced doubt about my materialist worldview for a while. The extremists' theories began seeming plausible to me. Few people know about this crisis of faith. However, there is one more rule I accept that mainstream science rejects. The moment possesses sentience and awareness. Human extinction appears to be its ultimate goal. As a man of science, I cannot allow fear to paralyze me. I must test my hypothesis through direct experimentation. You will now understand my disappearance and its purpose. Men my age have lower survival rates statistically. We can still find the answer if we take risks. Science will prevail through sacrifice. I've performed an orchidectomy on myself using proper surgical technique. By the time you read this, I should be within the moment's current spread zone. I wonder what people will think seeing a naked old man walking into danger. Is he insane or a religious fanatic? No pun intended regarding my condition. If I succeed, as I believe I will, stories will spread before I return. Hence this log entry serves as explanation. Stories will tell of a crazy old man whose faith made him immune. "I'm pretty sure this is a softball pitch from the management downstairs." Elwood said, arms crossed against his chest. Shara gave Elwood a sideways glance and raised an eyebrow, "Sure, though I doubt the period matters...."

Elwood flung his arms apart and the class resumed as normal, no one but Dale aware of what happened. The students immediately returned to taking notes as if nothing had occurred.

"That's your plan?" Shara asked, clearly unimpressed by the display.

Dale noticing he was a little behind in taking notes began writing in a hurry, his pencil scratching rapidly across the page.

"You're kidding me, right? That's a daytime creep! It's not even 3 am when the veil between worlds is thinnest. That's some creepy shit, I don't care what you say about technique."

As they were leaving through the wall, Elwood spun around and made a bitch-slapping motion with his clawed hand. Dale grunted and his head jerked forward, loose tangles of hair at the back of this head flying up in the air. Her nose wrinkled as if he emitted an offensive odor.

Shara laughed at the petty cruelty of the moment.

The two demons waited outside the classroom for the end of period and Dale's emergence. "You know this would be so much easier in the nighttime when fear comes naturally..." Shara said, bored with the daylight approach.

"Yeah but that's not my style, never has been." Elwood said defensively. "You get more *genuine* results during the day when people's guards are down.
